note: Primary sources opened via WebFetch unless access_level says 'search-summary'. 'classes_affected' uses original class numbers 1-6; M1/M2/M3/B0 are the revised-taxonomy ids.

sources.title: CoIn: Counting the Invisible Reasoning Tokens in Commercial Opaque LLM APIs
sources.relevance: Provider-side token-count inflation auditing; confirms the covered overcharge direction and that client under-payment is not considered.

sources.title: Invisible Tokens, Visible Bills: The Urgent Need to Audit Hidden Operations in Opaque LLM Services
sources.relevance: Formalizes provider quantity-inflation and quality-downgrade; explicitly does not address dishonest clients.

sources.title: Token Inflation: How Dishonest Providers Can Overcharge for Large Language Model Usage
sources.relevance: Measures provider over-report margin (tokenization ambiguity ~50.85%, hidden-reasoning inflation ~1469%) and names cancellation undercounting; ours is the unstudied mirror (client under-report).

sources.title: Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs
sources.relevance: Studies LLM prompt caching as a privacy/timing side channel (global cache sharing across 7 providers), not billing evasion; shows the LLM-cache mechanism is studied for a different goal.

sources.title: The single-packet attack: making remote race-conditions 'local'
sources.relevance: Generic HTTP/2 technique for limit-overrun web race conditions; baseline prior art for the credit/quota-decrement race (B0) and the reason old Class 4 is not novel.

sources.title: CVE-2026-31873 — Tyk API Gateway non-atomic quota check/decrement race
sources.relevance: Real recent CVE (CVSS 7.5): Redis GET-then-DECR non-atomic quota race, concurrency multiplies the allowance — exactly the credit/quota-decrement race; kills old Class 4 as a distinct class.

sources.title: The Cancellation Tax: Your Inference Bill After the User Hits Stop
sources.relevance: Documents the stream-abort accounting gap (decode loop continues after disconnect; Paid-to-Delivered Ratio) but frames it as honest operator over-pay, not adversarial client evasion.

sources.title: Streaming requests may refund all pre-consumed quota when final usage is missing after client disconnect (new-api #5235)
sources.relevance: A deployed LLM gateway: pre-consumed quota is fully refunded when the final usage block is missing after client disconnect — the client-exploitable stream-abort evasion in the wild (dated 2026-06-01).

sources.title: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
sources.relevance: Mass-assignment / property tampering (e.g. tier:premium, price) — the generic, mature vulnerability that old Class 5 rebrands; basis for killing Class 5.

sources.title: API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization
sources.relevance: The #1 API risk; forging plan/entitlement metadata to reach higher-tier models is BOLA/BFLA applied to model routing.

sources.title: Semantic Caching for LLMs: How to Cut Token Spend with AI Gateways
sources.relevance: Confirms a gateway cache hit makes no LLM call and burns zero tokens/quota, with shared cross-user caches — the LLM-specific hook (and risk) for M3.

sources.title: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
sources.relevance: The generic principle behind Class 2; establishes that client-declared trust is a decades-old weakness, so novelty must come from the LLM token-metering instantiation + measurement.

sources.title: Idempotency keys / safe retries (Stripe pattern; IETF HTTP idempotency-key draft)
sources.relevance: Billing idempotency (replay returns stored response without re-charge) is a solved standard; weakens Class 3's 'replay without new billing' angle.

sources.title: Token-count / billing discrepancy reports (AWS re:Post, Google AI forum, OpenAI community, litellm cost-discrepancy docs)
sources.relevance: Establishes that token-count mismatch is real and LLM-specific but always framed as honest discrepancy, never as client-side exploitation.

sources.title: LLMjacking: stolen cloud AI credentials used to run inference on victims' bills
sources.relevance: Client-side LLM abuse via stolen credentials (victim pays) — a different threat model from a legitimate-but-dishonest client, clarifying our quadrant.

sources.title: Denial-of-Wallet / Economic Denial of Sustainability against LLM APIs (OWASP LLM10 Unbounded Consumption; DoW reviews)
sources.relevance: Attacker inflates a victim's bill (availability/economic exhaustion) — the covered 'client-dishonest, inflate cost' cell, distinct from our 'evade cost' cell.

sources.title: Refunded but Rewarded: The Double Dip Attack on Cashback Reward Engines
sources.relevance: Generic refund/reconciliation abuse; context for the refund-on-missing-usage instance of M1 (new-api #5235) and for the false-positive 'reconciliation bug' check.
